inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing table: 'Operating company... professional services/broker' falls under the general operating-company row, not the bank/insurer row -- Aon is a capital-light fee-and-commission broker/advisor that carries NO underwriting risk and NO policyholder deposits/float on its balance sheet; it is economically a professional-services firm, not an insurer, despite the industry label. Confirmed against Analysis JSON business_model: 'capital-light broker/advisor that earns commissions and fees' with no underwriting or reserve liabilities. This is a fresh build -- no prior DCF exists for AON. PENDING USI ACQUISITION ($17B, ~14.5x synergized EBITDA, ~$3B USI revenue, $395M targeted run-rate EBITDA synergies, announced 2026-08-31, expected to close Q4 2026, financed with $13.5B bonds + $4B term loan = ~$17.5B new debt) is built into the BASE case balance sheet and flows: net_debt of $31,405M = Q2-2026 actual net debt ($13,905M) + $17,500M new debt raised to fund the deal (financing already completed per Analysis JSON 'recent_developments' 2026-09 bond offering). This pro-forma net debt against a fully-synergized combined EBITDA estimate (Aon standalone adj-EBITDA ~$5,399M FY2025 + USI synergized EBITDA ~$1,172M = ~$6,571M) implies ~4.78x leverage, which ties almost exactly to management's disclosed '~4.8x EBITDA at close' -- cross-check that validates both the net-debt and USI-EBITDA estimates used here. total_debt is shown as net_debt+cash for consistency (32,467 = 31,405+1,062); the engine only uses net_debt. Revenue path models USI as a ~15% partial-year stub added to FY2026 (Q4 2026 close) and a full first-year consolidation step-up in FY2027 (growth_rates jumps from 7.6% to 19.0%) rather than as a separate M&A line-item, because the engine takes a single growth-rate path off base_revenue; this is a modelling simplification and materially affects only the phasing, not the terminal value. EBITDA margin path is built as Aon's own adjusted-EBITDA basis (GAAP operating income + SBC expense + D&A/amortization of acquired intangibles added back, per section 2 of owner-fcf.md, since sbc_pct_path and da_pct_path are subtracted separately by the engine) -- FY2025 base of 31.4% cross-checks closely against Aon's own disclosed 'adjusted operating margin' of 32.4% for FY2025. D&A/amortization is large relative to capex ($623M vs $263M FY2025) because Aon is a serial acquirer with substantial acquired customer-relationship and technology intangible amortization (NFP 2024, USI from Q4 2026) -- this is structural, not a one-off, and rises further post-USI. Historical growth-rate selection: equity CAGR is NOT usable here (shareholders' equity was negative FY2022-23 from aggressive buybacks, then jumped to $9.35B FY2024-25 mostly from NFP-related equity issuance/retained earnings, not organic compounding -- same pattern flagged for Visa in MEMORY.md: 'FCF CAGR not equity CAGR (buybacks)'). Revenue 3yr/5yr CAGR (11.2%/9.2%) is used as the historical growth anchor, cross-checked against management's own mid-single-digit organic growth guidance plus disclosed M&A contribution. Owner-FCF CAGR (2.3%/3.8%) is far below revenue/NI CAGR -- flagged in historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning -- reflecting FY2024's NFP-integration cash drag and FY2021's COVID-recovery trough as the base years, not a deteriorating underlying FCF conversion; FY2025 owner-FCF margin of 15.0% is back near the FY2022-23 range of ~19%, which is why the forward build anchors margin expansion off FY2025 rather than off the trailing CAGR. Interest income NOT stripped -- Aon is a large net-debt company (net debt >> cash) both before and after USI, so there is no material net-cash pile to double-count. Buyback pace: FY2026 guided at 'at least $1B' (already exceeded via $600M in Q2 alone per Analysis JSON) but management has explicitly signalled buybacks will moderate near-term to prioritize USI-related debt paydown; buyback_cash of $1,000M reflects the guided FY2026 minimum, understood as a transitional trough, not the run-rate once leverage normalizes -- share count is held FLAT throughout per the SBC-charged-once rule (section 1 of owner-fcf.md) regardless of the buyback pace, since SBC is fully expensed in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is NOT computable/usable: shareholders' equity was negative FY2022 (-$429M) and FY2023 (-$742M) from a decade-plus of aggressive buybacks, then jumped to $6,121M FY2024 and $9,352M FY2025 mostly via NFP-related equity issuance and retained earnings -- a mechanical, not organic, series. Owner-FCF CAGR (3yr 2.3%, 5yr 3.8%) diverges sharply (>60%) from revenue CAGR (11.2%/9.2%) and NI CAGR (12.6%/13.4%): FY2024's owner-FCF was depressed by NFP integration cash costs and FY2021 (the 5yr base year) was a COVID-recovery trough, so the CAGR understates the current run-rate -- FY2025 owner-FCF margin (15.0%) is back close to the FY2022-23 range (~19%). Revenue CAGR, cross-checked against management's mid-single-digit organic growth guidance plus disclosed M&A contribution (NFP, pending USI), is used as the growth anchor instead of owner-FCF CAGR or equity CAGR.

base.narrative: USI closes on schedule (Q4 2026) and integration runs broadly to plan alongside the NFP integration Aon is already most of the way through. FY2026 organic growth lands at the guided mid-single digits (5%) with a partial-quarter USI contribution; FY2027 sees the first full year of USI consolidated plus continued AON organic growth in the mid-single digits, decelerating gradually toward a 3% terminal rate as the combined entity matures. EBITDA margin expands steadily (71-80bps/yr through FY2026-27 per guidance, moderating thereafter) as the 3x3 Plan's Aon Business Services shared-services program and the ~$280M of USI cost synergies phase in over roughly 3 years post-close. Leverage (~4.8x at close) declines gradually via FCF-funded debt paydown, buybacks stay near the guided FY2026 minimum ($1B) before resuming a more typical pace once leverage normalizes (buybacks are value-neutral in this model regardless -- SBC is charged once via the flat share count). Cash tax rate holds near the recent 24% effective cash rate; no valuation-allowance or one-off benefit assumed.

bull.narrative: USI integration delivers ahead of the $395M synergy target and faster than the 3-year phasing assumed in base, echoing Aon's largely successful NFP playbook; cross-sell between Risk Capital and Human Capital (the 'Aon United' platform) and AI/data-analytics-driven productivity gains (Aon Business Services) push margin expansion above the guided 70-80bps/yr. Organic growth benefits from a firmer P&C/reinsurance pricing cycle (a reversal of the 2025-26 softening) plus stronger cross-sell into the enlarged US middle-market client base. Deleveraging happens faster than the ~2-year target, allowing buybacks to resume at a more typical pace (historically ~$1.5-2.5B/yr) sooner, and the credit-rating outlook stabilizes rather than deteriorating.

bear.narrative: USI still closes (regulatory blockage is treated as low-probability given the deal's diversifying, non-top-3-consolidating nature per Analysis JSON) but integration is materially harder than NFP: culture clash and system integration problems mean synergies run well behind the $395M target and take 5+ years rather than 3, while a sustained soft P&C/reinsurance pricing cycle (record $785B global reinsurance capital cited in Analysis JSON) compresses organic commission growth even with flat exposure units. Elevated ~4.8x leverage does not decline on schedule -- S&P's negative outlook crystallizes into an actual downgrade, raising the cost of the next refinancing and forcing capital returns toward zero for several years as free cash flow is redirected entirely to debt paydown. EBITDA margin compresses in FY2026-27 (integration and transaction costs, amortization step-up from USI intangibles) before a slow recovery.

scenario_narratives.base: USI closes on schedule and integrates broadly to plan; steady margin expansion continues per the 3x3 Plan and guided synergy phasing; leverage normalizes gradually and buybacks resume at a moderate pace.
scenario_narratives.bull: USI integration outperforms (echoing the NFP playbook), pricing cycle firms, AI/analytics-driven margin gains beat guidance, and faster deleveraging lets capital returns resume sooner.
scenario_narratives.bear: USI still closes but integration is materially harder than NFP, synergies run late and light, a sustained soft pricing cycle compresses organic growth, and leverage stays elevated long enough to trigger an actual ratings downgrade, crowding out buybacks for years.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised from the 15% house default to 25% (bull correspondingly trimmed to 25%) because AON is simultaneously (a) closing and integrating a $17B transformational acquisition while (b) still digesting the 2024 NFP deal, (c) has nearly doubled leverage to ~4.8x EBITDA -- already triggering a negative S&P outlook revision -- and (d) faces a softening P&C/reinsurance pricing cycle independent of the deal. This is genuine, disclosed, near-term financial-risk stacking (not merely normal cyclicality), which is exactly the situation owner-fcf.md section 3 flags for raising the bear weight (covenant/leverage pressure, integration risk on an unproven scale). It is not raised further because the deal is diversifying rather than a top-3 consolidation (lower antitrust risk than the blocked 2021 WTW merger) and Aon's NFP integration track record to date has been reasonably clean.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Aon is a capital-light, high-margin insurance/reinsurance broker and HR/benefits consulting firm valued on an owner-FCF DCF. The business itself is a durable, moderately cyclical fee-and-commission compounder with real moats (switching costs, scale/data advantages, global one-stop-shop breadth). The near-term investment case is dominated by a single, large, disclosed capital-allocation and integration bet: the pending $17B USI acquisition, which nearly doubles leverage to ~4.8x EBITDA at close and stacks a second major integration (USI) on top of the still-ongoing NFP integration. The stock's ~28% drawdown from its 52-week high to a price near the 52-week low reflects the market pricing meaningful execution and leverage risk into this deal. The valuation here bakes the pro-forma post-close balance sheet and USI's revenue/EBITDA contribution into the base case (the deal is financed and expected imminently), while using an elevated bear weight (25% vs the 15% house default) to reflect the genuine, currently-elevated financial and integration risk rather than pretending the risk away with a lower discount rate stacked on top of probability weighting.
key_risks_to_valuation: USI integration risk on top of an already-in-progress NFP integration -- two large, simultaneous integrations is a real execution burden

Leverage nearly doubling to ~4.8x EBITDA at close, with a negative S&P outlook already in place -- an actual ratings downgrade would raise refinancing costs across a large, newly-issued debt stack (7 tranches, 3-30yr)

Capital returns (buybacks, historically ~39% net share reduction over 12 years) are being deliberately curtailed near-term to fund debt paydown, removing a lever that has supported EPS growth and the stock's valuation for over a decade
Softening P&C/reinsurance pricing cycle (record ~$785B global reinsurance capital) is a headwind to organic commission growth independent of the deal
Regulatory approval of the USI deal, while less contentious than the blocked 2021 Aon-WTW merger, remains a closing condition and is not guaranteed on the expected Q4 2026 timeline

The revenue path models USI as a growth-rate step-up rather than an explicit M&A line, which is a modelling simplification -- if the deal is delayed or falls through, FY2026-27 revenue and margin would be materially below the base case shown here (this is close to what the bear case, at 25% weight, represents)
